categories.main_business_segments: Cirrus Logic operates as a single reportable segment but reports revenue in two primary product lines: Audio and High-Performance Mixed-Signal (HPMS) products. Audio products include amplifiers, codecs, smart codecs, analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog converters, and standalone digital signal processors. HPMS products encompass camera controllers, haptics and sensing solutions, and battery and power ICs, primarily for smartphones but also for automotive, industrial, and imaging applications.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company specializes in low-power, high-precision mixed-signal processing, integrating analog and digital technologies into custom and general market integrated circuits. Cirrus Logic is a fabless semiconductor company, outsourcing wafer fabrication to foundries like TSMC and GlobalFoundries, and assembly/testing to third-party vendors. Their products often combine proprietary hardware with embedded software and algorithms, leveraging both internal and third-party intellectual property.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Cirrus Logic's key customers are leading global electronics manufacturers, with Apple Inc. accounting for approximately 89% of total net sales in fiscal 2025. The company serves markets including smartphones, laptops, tablets, AR/VR headsets, wearables, home theater, automotive entertainment, and professional audio systems. Their products are typically specified by end customers and may be purchased directly or through contract manufacturers and distributors.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates globally, with principal facilities in Austin, Texas and Edinburgh, Scotland, and offices in the United States, United Kingdom, China, Taiwan, South Korea, Japan, and Singapore. In fiscal 2025, 99% of net sales were international, with significant revenue from China, India, Hong Kong, South Korea, and Vietnam. Manufacturing and supply chain operations are concentrated in Asia, particularly Taiwan and Singapore.
categories.supply_chain_position: Cirrus Logic is positioned as a fabless, upstream-to-midstream supplier in the semiconductor value chain, focusing on the design and development of integrated circuits and mixed-signal solutions. The company outsources all wafer fabrication, assembly, and testing to third-party foundries and subcontractors, and its components are integrated into end products by OEMs and contract manufacturers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategically, Cirrus Logic aims to maintain leadership in smartphone audio, increase HPMS content in smartphones, and expand into new applications and markets leveraging its audio and mixed-signal expertise. R&D is focused on developing new products for principal markets, advancing process technologies, and supporting customer integration from concept to production. The company is also investing in emerging opportunities such as laptops and general market components, with a strong emphasis on innovation and differentiation.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through the sale of proprietary integrated circuits and components to OEMs, contract manufacturers, and distributors. Revenue is recognized upon transfer of goods, with most sales made via short-term purchase orders rather than long-term contracts. The company also benefits from government R&D credits, particularly in the UK, which offset R&D expenses.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Cirrus Logic faces intense competition from semiconductor suppliers such as AKM Semiconductor, Analog Devices, Qualcomm, Realtek, Renesas, Skyworks, STMicroelectronics, Synaptics, and Texas Instruments. While no single competitor covers all product lines, many have greater resources and broader portfolios. Cirrus Logic differentiates through its focus on low-power, high-precision mixed-signal solutions and strong customer relationships, particularly with Apple.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In fiscal 2025, Cirrus Logic reported net sales of $1.90 billion, up 6% from $1.79 billion in 2024, with net income of $331.5 million and a gross margin of 52.5%. The company has a strong balance sheet with $539.6 million in cash and cash equivalents and no outstanding debt under its $300 million revolving credit facility. Growth is driven by new product introductions, increased content in smartphones, and expansion into adjacent markets.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Cirrus Logic emphasizes its expertise in low-power, high-precision mixed-signal processing, enabling innovative user experiences in mobile and consumer devices. The company differentiates through highly integrated, programmable components, proprietary algorithms, and strong engineering partnerships with leading OEMs. Its solutions offer superior audio quality, advanced haptics, and efficient power management, supporting customer product differentiation across device tiers.
